speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; I see you present with gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history. To begin narrowing down the cause, can you describe the specific nature of your ataxia and which limbs are most affected?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you; since the clumsiness is predominantly on the right side, does this ataxia come on suddenly or develop gradually over time? Also, have you noticed any new weakness or numbness in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, this significantly raises the suspicion for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Has your vision changed, or have you experienced any confusion or speech difficulties? REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.
